value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for composing verified code without rewriting it
lets_workers: Write a small declarative recipe that wires prewritten, tested code nodes together, instead of writing new code for routine data steps.
Compile a recipe into a checked graph: unknown nodes, wrong port types, bad parameters, missing wiring and cycles are refused with typed diagnostics before anything runs.
Run a compiled recipe with no model calls, reuse the cached results of unchanged upstream steps, and prove that the emitted standalone Python gives byte-identical outputs.
Check that a local copy of the code matches this pack's pins: folder digest, module digests, node digests and built-in tests.
Compare a baseline recipe with a variant by their receipts, and propose a reviewed new node when the catalog lacks a capability.
flow: verify-tools checks a library checkout's code folder against the pins, once per sandbox.
compose-recipe turns a goal into a recipe candidate that compiles.
compile-recipe compiles a pinned recipe and records its plan digest.
run-recipe executes it with pinned inputs and records the receipt.
compare-runs compares a baseline and a variant by their receipts.
propose-node, then review-node by a different worker or a person, when no node fits.

related_packs.use: Validate a proposed node's test cases before anyone relies on them.
Measure the baseline before changing anything when comparing recipe variants.
Trial another composition tool against this one with a comparable trial.

value.title: Tool card: code composition tools
value.category_reason: A tool card pins the code's identity, license, interfaces and checks for the verbs that run it.
value.name: Code composition tools

tool_license.how_to_determine: Read pyproject.toml in the code folder and the library's LICENSE.

value.pin_reason: The code lives in this pack, so it is pinned by content, not by commit. Every digest in this pack was measured on the files that folder.sha256 covers. A code folder with another digest is a different tool until a new pack version pins it and verify-tools passes.
value.folder_rule: folder.sha256 is the library's pack-code digest: SHA-256 of `pack-code-v1` and a NUL byte, then the canonical JSON of the sorted [path, file SHA-256] pairs of every file under the code folder, skipping caches, virtual environments, build output and egg-info. The library build computes it from the files and the pack manifest repeats it, so a pin that no longer matches the code fails make check. To recompute it from a checkout's root: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts'); import build_packs as b; from pathlib import Path; print(b.code_digest(Path('packs/code-composition')))"
value.address_note: Use a checkout of this library whose code folder matches folder.sha256. If none does, end blocked and say so; do not substitute another source. The folder digest is what must match.
value.package_path_rule: Module names in this pack, such as compiler.py, are relative to the import package that pyproject.toml lists under [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages.

requires.lockfile: uv.lock in the code folder; install with uv sync --locked --all-groups there.

uses: Compile a declarative recipe into a checked graph of prewritten nodes (compiler.DeterministicCompiler.compile).
Emit a standalone Python module for a compiled plan (compiler.DeterministicCompiler.emit_python_from_plan).
Execute a compiled plan with a sub-graph cache and a SHA-256 receipt (runtime.DeterministicRuntime.execute).
List, verify and register prewritten nodes in a SQLite node database (registry.NodeDatabase).
Check one claimed seed task against its pins before running it (seed_worker.execute_seed_task).
Export the code's own Tessera-shaped seed nouns and tasks as an offline preview document (seed_pack.build_seed_pack).

interfaces.command_line: The code-composition console script that pyproject.toml declares under [project.scripts], with subcommands init, nodes, verify-nodes, seed-pack, compile, run, compose and demo.

make_targets.check: ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy in strict mode and pytest
make_targets.demo: verify all 18 nodes, compile and run the 3 recipes with the Python equivalence check, and show cached prefix reuse
make_targets.tessera-integration: the seed export against Tessera's real models, with TESSERA_DIR set to a prepared Tessera checkout

checks.command: make check demo, in the code folder
checks.result_at_pin: pass; pytest reports 41 passed and 2 skipped on Python 3.12.13 and 3.13.13 (the 2 Tessera tests skip without Tessera's environment)

checks.command: make tessera-integration TESSERA_DIR=<Tessera checkout at the commit above>, in the code folder

checks.result_at_pin: pass; the build recomputes the folder digest from the files, and the code's own tests, run by its CI job, check the runtime, node and recipe pins against the code

value.measured: Measured on October 29, 2026 by the pack author in a library checkout on Linux, with Python 3.12.13 and 3.13.13 giving identical digests. A path-filtered CI job reruns these checks on every change to this pack. This is not independent verification.
cautions: Run code only from a checkout whose code folder matches folder.sha256 and passed verify-tools. Never execute source code copied out of a noun.
Node code and emitted Python run in the worker's own Python process; this is not a security sandbox.

Every subcommand except seed-pack creates or migrates a SQLite file at its --db path, and without --db uses CODE_COMPOSITION_DB or a default path under the current directory; seed-pack opens an existing file read-only. Pass a path inside the task workspace.

The compose subcommand calls a model endpoint when CODE_COMPOSITION_LLM_BASE_URL is set, and looks up earlier recipes in a Tessera deployment whenever TESSERA_URL is set, even with --offline. The verbs in this pack need neither; leave both unset.
Seed export provenance reads the library checkout's HEAD only when the code sits at the pinned path; a copy anywhere else must pass --source-commit.
value.install_policy: This card installs nothing. A worker checks out the library, confirms the code folder's digest and installs its locked dependencies in its own task workspace under its execution policy.

value.title: Compiler and runtime: entry points, checks and module digests of the pinned code
value.category_reason: Pins the exact compiler and runtime modules that every compile and run verb must use.
value.digest_rule: SHA-256 of each module file's bytes with CRLF line endings normalized to LF. The code's seed_worker module applies the same rule before it runs a seed task, and the code's own tests check these pins in CI.
compile_checks: Every step names a node in the node database; an unknown node id gets a close-match suggestion (node_not_found).

Governance lens: the node's source matches its code_sha256, the node carries the code's own verified status tag and no quarantine tag, and its SPDX license is one of Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, CC0-1.0, MIT (node_governance_failed).
Parameters: unknown names are refused, int refuses booleans, numeric bounds and string choices are enforced, and a required parameter without a default must be set (parameter_constraint_failed).

Edges: both ports exist, with a suggestion on a typo (port_not_found); source and destination port types are exactly equal (port_type_mismatch); an input port takes at most one edge (duplicate_input_wiring).

Unwired inputs of root steps, and inputs listed in external_inputs as step.port, become graph entry inputs; an unwired required input on any other step is refused with its compatible upstream outputs (missing_required_input).
Order: a deterministic Kahn topological sort in declaration order; a cycle is refused with its exact path (cycle_detected).
Each step gets a Merkle fingerprint of its node digest, resolved parameters, entry ports and upstream fingerprints, so renaming steps does not change it and any upstream change does.
Warnings, not errors: isolated_step and dangling_transform.
runtime_behavior: Zero model calls; every receipt records llm_tokens_at_runtime 0.
A step's cached output is reused when its fingerprint and input digest match; cached and fresh outputs are both checked against the declared port types.
Entry inputs are matched by port name, or by step.port when a port name appears on more than one root step; a missing or wrongly typed entry input is refused (execution_input_invalid).
Receipts carry recipe, plan, node, input and output digests, the executed and cached steps, and a receipt digest.
With the equivalence check on, the emitted standalone module runs on the same inputs and must give byte-identical step and terminal outputs.
value.trust_note: Execution is in-process and trusts the verified nodes. It is not a sandbox for unreviewed code.

value.title: How to compose verified code without rewriting it
value.category_reason: A reusable method with its guardrails.
principles: Compose instead of rewriting: a recipe names catalog node ids, wires their ports with edges and sets bounded parameters. It contains no code.
Read signatures, not source: the catalog's one-line signatures are enough to write a recipe.
Compile before running. The compiler refuses unknown nodes, wrong port types, bad parameters, missing wiring and cycles with a typed error code, the step, the port and often a suggestion.
Repair from diagnostics: change the step, port or parameter the compiler names. Never work around a refusal by writing code into a recipe or a node.
Run only pinned, verified code: a checkout whose code folder matches the tool card's folder digest and passed verify-tools. Never execute source code copied out of a noun.
Runs make no model calls, and every receipt shows it.
Pin everything: tool folder digest, node digests, recipe digest and input digest. A change to any of them is a new run, not an update to an old receipt.
Change one thing at a time. A variant that keeps upstream steps unchanged reuses their cached outputs, so the comparison is cheap and its differences are attributable.
Grow the catalog deliberately. When no node fits, propose one with exact-value tests; a different worker or a person reviews it, and adding it to the pack's code is the owner's decision.

repair_codes.node_not_found: Use a catalog node id; the diagnostic suggests the closest one.
repair_codes.parameter_constraint_failed: Fix the parameter's name, type, bounds or choice.
repair_codes.port_not_found: Use one of the ports the diagnostic lists.
repair_codes.port_type_mismatch: Wire a port of exactly the same type, or insert a node that converts it.
repair_codes.missing_required_input: Wire one of the compatible upstream outputs the diagnostic lists.
repair_codes.duplicate_input_wiring: Keep one edge per input port.
repair_codes.unknown_step: Make every edge name declared steps.
repair_codes.duplicate_step_id: Give every step a unique id.
repair_codes.invalid_external_input: Write external inputs as step.port for a declared step and port.
repair_codes.conflicting_external_input: Do not list a wired port as an external input.
repair_codes.node_governance_failed: Stop: the node fails the governance lens and must not be used.
repair_codes.execution_input_invalid: At run time: supply every entry input with its declared port type, using step.port when a port name is ambiguous.
